verdict.rationale: Amplitude's docs say a flag can carry as many variants as you want, which makes flags multivariate rather than boolean. Each flag can also attach a JSON-coded payload of variables that remotely changes behavior without a code change, which covers dynamic configuration. missing for 10: explicit documentation of typed string/number config values and how SDKs read payloads, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve multivariate flags and dynamic configuration values (strings, numbers, JSON), not just booleans

citations.quote: You can add as many variants as you want to a flag.
A payload is a JSON-coded set of variables that can remotely change flags and experiments without a manual code change.
Run A/B, multivariate, and bandit tests
